case_title.value: RAKESH & ANR. v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH

quotes.text: RAKESH & ANR. v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
The two appellants alongwith another accused caused the death of PW11's uncle by assaulting him with sharp edged weapons.

The appellants challenged their conviction before this Court inter a/ia on grounds 1) that the ocular evidence was contradictory to the medical evidence as regards the time of death; and 2) that the alleged eye witness PW.11 was closely related to the victim and none of the independent witnesses examined by the prosecution supported its case to the extent that PW.11 could be present on the place of occurrence at the relevant time.

neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that two appellants, along with another accused, caused the death of the victim by assaulting him with sharp edged weapons. The victim was taken to the hospital where he was examined by a doctor and declared dead. The accused were arrested, and the weapons used in the crime were recovered on their disclosure statements. The trial court convicted the two appellants under Section 302 IPC and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for life. The conviction was upheld by the High Court. The appellants challenged their conviction on the grounds that the ocular evidence was contradictory to the medical evidence regarding the time of death and that the alleged eye witness was closely related to the victim. The Supreme Court held that the ocular evidence had primacy unless it was established that oral evidence was totally irreconcilable with the medical evidence. The Court also noted that the witness's testimony was trustworthy and that the prosecution case was supported by other evidence, including the statements of the Investigating Officer and the recovery of weapons.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the two appellants, alongwith another accused, caused the death of PW11's uncle by assaulting him with sharp edged weapons. All the weapons allegedly used in the crime were recovered on the disclosure statements made by the appellants and the other accused. PW.8 conducted post-mortem on the body of the deceased and found three incised wounds on the body, one on the neck, one on the chest and another in the abdomen, all caused by sharp edged weapons. PW11 testified to have witnessed the incident. The prosecution also emphasized that the FIR was lodged promptly and with all details, indicating the truth of the version.

legal_principle_applied.value: The ocular evidence would have primacy unless it is established that oral evidence is totally irreconcilable with the medical evidence. Where the medical evidence goes so far that it completely rules out all possibility of the ocular evidence if proved, the ocular evidence may be disbelieved.

Prompt and early reporting of the occurrence by the informant with all its vivid details gives an assurance regarding truth of its version.
